title: Design System: Event Pilot — The Inclusive Celebration Almanac

components.name: Primary Action Button
components.description: Solid marigold action button for primary workflows such as adding expenses or generating a planning proposal. Deep ink text is used on the marigold background for improved contrast.
components.css: .ep-btn-primary { background: #D97706; color: #1C1917; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(217, 119, 6, 0.2); } .ep-btn-primary:hover { background: #B45309; color: #FFFFFF; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ep-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1C1917; outline-offset: 3px; } .ep-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.55; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; }

components.name: Coupon-Style Status Stamp
components.description: Tactile coupon-style label for states explicitly recorded by the user or application. It does not independently verify a vendor, booking, or payment.
components.css: .ep-badge-coupon { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #FFEDD5; color: #9A3412; border: 1px dashed #9A3412; border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.03em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Ledger Card
components.description: Clean elevated card for budget items, milestones, and vendor records, using a white surface, fine border, and restrained shadow.
components.css: .ep-card-ledger { background: #FFFFFF; color: #1C1917; border: 1px solid #E7DFD5; border-radius: 12px; padding: 20px; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(28, 25, 23, 0.04); }

narrative.overview: Event Pilot is an editorial event-planning studio inspired by the warmth, organization, and chronological clarity of an almanac. Warm ivory surfaces, deep ink typography, restrained marigold and terracotta accents, and carefully structured ledgers turn planning complexity into a clear and welcoming experience. Panchang, Muhurtam, auspicious-date information, and other tradition-specific features are optional and context-aware; the product never assumes a user's religion, cultural identity, or preferred traditions.
keyCharacteristics: Warm papyrus canvas (#FDFBF7) that evokes tactile stationery without sacrificing digital clarity.
Distinctive editorial typography pairing Eczar display headings with readable Plus Jakarta Sans and JetBrains Mono for aligned numerical information.
Stepped, index-inspired navigation that supports orientation without constraining responsive layouts.
Coupon-style status stamps that represent explicitly recorded user or application states rather than independent verification.
Layered proposal comparisons that let users review AI additions and changes before accepting them.
Responsive information hierarchy that keeps planning efficient across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
Inclusive event setup that makes cultural and tradition-specific preferences optional rather than assumed.

rules.name: The Functional Accent Rule
rules.body: Marigold (#D97706) and Terracotta (#C2410C) primarily emphasize interactive actions, selection states, navigation, and meaningful planning information. Avoid arbitrary decorative use. Pair each foreground and background combination according to verified contrast requirements.

rules.name: The Tabular Truth Rule
rules.body: Use tabular numerals for financial figures, guest counts, dates, and aligned numerical columns where they improve scanning. All financial arithmetic, date calculations, countdowns, and capacity checks must use deterministic application logic.

rules.name: The Paper Foundation Rule
rules.body: Express elevation through tonal paper shifts, delicate borders (#E7DFD5), and restrained shadows rather than heavy visual effects.

rules.name: The Inclusive Almanac Rule
rules.body: The almanac is a visual and organizational inspiration, not a default religious or cultural assumption. Tradition-specific calendars, Muhurtam, auspicious-date guidance, and rituals must be optional and informed by the user's stated context.

rules.name: The Recorded State Rule
rules.body: Status labels must reflect information explicitly recorded by the user or established by a reliable application operation. Never imply independent vendor verification, confirmed booking, or payment processing without supporting evidence.

rules.name: The Responsive Workspace Rule
rules.body: Keep navigation, summaries, and actions proportional to the available viewport. Use a persistent action bar only when a workflow benefits from it, and never force the full desktop shell onto narrow screens.

dos: Do use INR (₹) as the default event currency and format it appropriately, for example ₹2,50,000.
Do display the currency selected for each event and never mix currencies or silently convert between them.
Do verify foreground/background contrast for all actual component states; target WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements.
Do use tabular numerals for aligned financial amounts, guest counts, dates, and other relevant numerical data.
Do show clear loading states and progress feedback during Gemini proposal generation.
Do preserve existing user data when AI generation, validation, or saving fails.
Do make AI changes reviewable and require explicit user acceptance before applying them.
Do use badges only for statuses actually recorded by the user or established by reliable application behavior.
Do pair status colors with text labels or meaningful icons.
Do keep navigation and action placement responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
Do respect reduced-motion preferences and maintain keyboard accessibility.
Do keep guest personal information and dietary details out of AI requests by default.
Do make tradition-specific planning features optional and context-aware.
donts: Don't assume a religious tradition, ritual, calendar, or auspicious-date preference for every event.
Don't use cold generic SaaS blues, purple AI gradients, or decorative neon sparkles.
Don't label vendors as verified or bookings as confirmed unless the exact status is supported by recorded information or reliable evidence.
Don't imply that Event Pilot processed or independently verified a deposit when the user only recorded its status.
Don't hard-code INR as the only supported event currency.
Don't combine amounts from different currencies or silently convert between currencies.
Don't use white text on Marigold Amber (#D97706) without verified contrast; use Deep Ink (#1C1917) for the default primary button text.
Don't rely on color alone to communicate statuses, errors, selection, or AI proposal differences.
Don't perform currency arithmetic, date arithmetic, or authoritative business-rule calculations inside LLM prompts.
Don't allow AI suggestions to silently overwrite existing plans; all changes must pass through an explicit review and acceptance step.
Don't crowd every screen with a fixed header, full navigation rail, multiple summary cards, and a permanent bottom action bar.
Don't hide essential financial, guest, or task information merely to simplify mobile layouts.
Don't sacrifice readability, keyboard access, or reduced-motion support for decorative effects.
